lines.text: In 2007, US regulators examined 110 firms running free-lunch investment seminars.

post.title: Free investment dinners: what regulators found in 110 exams
post.ig:
Regulators found every free investment dinner they checked was a sales pitch.
In a 2007 joint SEC/NASAA/FINRA review of 110 firms running free-lunch investment seminars, 100% of the seminars were sales presentations.
50% used exaggerated or misleading ads; 23% made possibly unsuitable recommendations.
FTC data: reported investment-scam losses hit $7.9 billion in 2025, up from $3.8 billion in 2022 (about double).
Regulators suggest checking any seller on FINRA BrokerCheck, the SEC adviser search (adviserinfo.sec.gov), or with your state regulator before you sign anything.
Sources: SEC/NASAA/FINRA 2007 report; FTC Consumer Sentinel.
News and education, not financial advice.
